title: tenant-network-replay-and-verification-tooling-prd-wip
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working PRD for a Network Change Replay & Verification Tooling feature for Private Deployments. The goal is to give customers and Red‑team operators deterministic verification of tenant-side network changes by producing replayable evidence bundles that can be both machine-verified and human-audited.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Customers with customer-managed networking frequently ask for reproducible audit artifacts that prove a configuration change did not alter the deployed traffic plane or data exfiltration boundaries.
- Current audit logs provide event traces but are hard to validate end‑to‑end: timestamps, async agents, and transient operator actions make root cause and rollforward/rollback proofs manual and error prone.
- We need a reproducible, tamper-resistant way to reconstruct the effective network state and show a deterministic diff between pre/post change traffic/evidence.

Non-goals:
- This does NOT replace full security postures (ids/ips) or forensic tooling.
- It is not a general packet capture platform — focus is on configuration and control-plane replay plus sampled telemetry for verification.

Users and personas:
- Platform/security engineer at customer: needs legally defensible evidence that a change respected isolation contracts.
- Redwood SRE/Operator: needs quick repro to validate a reported regression was caused by a customer change or by infra.
- Compliance reviewer / auditor: needs a human-readable report and cryptographic proof that logs have not been tampered with.

High-level feature summary:
1) Evidence bundle generation: when a tenant requests a change (via API/Console), produce an evidence bundle that contains: signed change metadata, ordered control-plane events, sampled telemetry (flow summaries, not full pcap), and service-level snapshots (routing tables, iptables/nft rules, BGP adjacencies) taken from both customer and Redwood operator views.
2) Deterministic replay engine: a sandboxed harness that can consume an evidence bundle and replay control-plane events to reconstruct effective state at two checkpoints (pre-change, post-change).
3) Diff & verification suite: machine checks (reachability matrix, ACL mismatch, route leaks) plus a human-facing verification report with 'assertions' that map to approval gates and compliance checks.
4) Immutable attestation: bundles are hashed and signed with customer KMS/HSM keys (where provided) and Redwood audit keys; signatures and chain-of-custody metadata stored in append-only ledger for retention/forensics.
5) Approval gate integration: for changes marked as high-impact, the change cannot be applied until a successful dry-run replay and verification report is produced (or an explicit override with higher-level approver).

Detailed behaviors and APIs:
- Submit change workflow: POST /v1/private/tenants/{id}/network-changes -> returns change-id, evidence-bundle-id, and pre-check tokens.
- Evidence bundle format: newline-delimited JSON with top-level sections: metadata, event_stream (ordered), snapshots, sampled_telemetry, signatures, human_summary.txt.
- Replay API: POST /v1/replay/run with evidence_bundle_id + replay_profile (fast/strict) -> returns replay-job-id, stdout/stderr artifacts, and a verification status {PASS, WARN, FAIL}.
- Diff assertions: JSON array of assertions that the client can attach to approval gates (e.g., "no-new-egress-to-unowned-cidr") with severity and auto-fail rules.

Security and compliance:
- Support BYOK: customers can provide an external KMS key to sign bundles. When absent, Redwood signs and the bundle is marked as operator-signed only.
- Audit ledger: hashes of bundles (SHA-256) are appended to a tamper-evident ledger; ledger supports export for legal subpoena and periodic notarization snapshot.
- Data minimization: sampled telemetry is configurable per-tenant; default sampling is flow-level aggregates for last 30s around the change, retained only for the retention window.
- Access controls: evidence bundles are accessible only to tenant admins and Redwood SREs with justification logs; every access creates an access-event entry.

Operational considerations:
- Storage estimate: average bundle ~3–12 MB depending on sampling; plan for 10k bundles/month for early enterprise tenants => ~120 GB/mo, with lifecycle policies to cold storage after 90 days.
- Replay compute: sandboxed containerized harness with CPU-bound deterministic simulation; each replay should target < 2 minutes on typical small bundle. Parallelization required for bursty approval workflows.
- Cost controls: customers can opt into automatic pruning policies and compressed archive storage; Redwood may charge for long-term evidentiary retention (>1 year).

UI / Console UX:
- Change details page includes a "Generate evidence bundle" button, preview of assertions, and expected verification time.
- Verification report page shows pass/fail, assertion results, side-by-side routing table snapshots, and a downloadable signed bundle (zip).
- Approvals: change forms expose a list of required assertions; approvers can review machine checks and attached notes.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Evidence bundle v1 schema designed and stable; producers (agents) implemented for the most common customer-managed networking (VPC peering, route tables, firewall rules).
- Replay harness can reconstruct snapshot state and run the baseline assertion set (reachability and ACL mismatch) with >95% deterministic parity in internal tests.
- Console displays verification report and prevents gated changes when assertion set contains auto-fail.
- Signatures are produced and ledgers capture bundle hashes; storage lifecycle policy in place.

Rollout plan and milestones (Q2–Q3 2025):
- Sprint 1 (4w): schema design, API contracts, CI replay harness skeleton.
- Sprint 2 (6w): implement agents to capture snapshots (agent for customer-edge connector + control-plane adapter), storage pipeline, basic verification rules.
- Alpha (2w): internal + 2 pilot customers (one mid-market, one enterprise) for feedback on bundle content and UI.
- Beta (6w): stability, perf tuning, authorization workflows, KMS integration.
- GA: support contract options for long-term retention and forensic export.

Open questions / risks / tradeoffs:
- Sampling vs. full capture: legal teams may request full packet capture for certain cases; need policy + opt-in pricing.
- Determinism: control-plane event ordering across distributed agents may produce non-determinism; we need a reconciliation layer that normalizes timestamps and defines conflict resolution rules.
- Liability: what level of warranty do we provide for assertions? We should bake clear T&Cs and limited warranty language into the offering.
- Performance: replay duration for large enterprise bundles may be substantial; define timeout/queueing policies and SLA expectations.

Dependencies:
- Private-deploy CP agent work (agent snapshot endpoints) — infra/agents team (ENG: Mei Wong).
- KMS/HSM support from security team — (SEC: Omar Hassan).
- Console UI components for verification pages — frontend (ENG: Rafael Kim).

Next steps (short-term):
- Finalize schema and publish API contract doc (owner: Aisha) by 2025-03-12.
- Kickoff replay harness spike with infra team (owner: Rafael) — 2w.
- Confirm legal language and retention SLAs with legal & finance (owner: product ops).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft focused on technical feasibility and early UX; please flag areas where we are being too prescriptive about signature/ledger implementations or where customer privacy concerns might require more conservative defaults.
- Slack thread: #priv-deploy-replay for ongoing discussion; link above.
